experiment.hypothesis: We investigate whether conceptual computations in decoder-only language models operate inside low-dimensional causal subspaces that are strongly steerable layers before becoming decodable through the Direct Logit Lens, a General-Corpus Ridge Tuned Lens, a true KL-Minimizing General-Corpus Tuned Lens (exact Belrose et al. objective), or a Domain-Trained Tuned Lens. Across 4 distinct model families (Qwen3-1.7B, SmolLM2-1.7B, Mistral-7B-v0.1, OLMo-2-1124-7B; 1.7B-7.3B), 4 comparative domains (2,688 held-out cross-lexicon pairs), 1-position vs. sustained per-step multi-token generation steering, and a natural-language real scientific abstract classification benchmark, we test Paired-Swap ACE against all 6 baselines.

setup.train_test_split: disjoint 8 train / 8 unseen test entities (56 ordered pairs/lexicon x 3 cross-lexicons = 168/domain)

analysis.abstract_text: Interpretability tools routinely assume that if a transformer represents a concept linearly in its residual stream, that concept can be decoded by projecting intermediate activations through the unembedding matrix (Logit Lens) or a trained affine translator (Tuned Lens). Evaluating 4 distinct open-weight model families spanning 1.7B to 7.3B parameters (Qwen3-1.7B, SmolLM2-1.7B, Mistral-7B, OLMo-2-7B) across 4 real-world comparative domains and 2,688 strictly held-out cross-lexicon entity pairs (100% single-token across all 4 tokenizers), we test this assumption against Paired-Swap Algorithmic Core Extraction (ACE) and five strong baselines (Direct Logit Lens, General-Corpus Tuned Lens, Domain Residual-Affine Tuned Lens, Contrastive Activation Addition [CAA], and L2 Logistic Probes). Across 16 (model, domain) cells, peak 1D causal steering emerges where ACE linear readout (mean AUC 0.765) consistently exceeds Direct Logit Lens (0.727, gap +0.039, Wilcoxon p=0.065), KL-Minimizing General-Corpus Tuned Lens (0.638, gap +0.127, p=0.011), and Ridge General-Corpus Tuned Lens (0.693, p=0.037) and significantly outperforms Domain Tuned Lens (0.708, gap +0.057, p=4.67e-02), while operating largely orthogonal to the unembedding contrast vector (mean |cos(q_l*, dW_U)| = 0.140). On 1D causal necessity (Flip-1D across unseen cross-lexicons), ACE achieves mean AUC reversal +0.235 — significantly outperforming random controls (-0.001, p=1.53e-05), CAA (+0.170, p=1.53e-04; 14/16 cells), and L2 Logistic Probes (+0.179, p=3.81e-03; 13/16 cells). Most strikingly, on causal sufficiency (Keep-1D — deleting 2,047-4,095 orthogonal dimensions and retaining only the single 1D ACE coordinate), Keep-1D outperforms the full unperturbed model in 16/16 cells (sign-test p=1.53e-05; mean AUC 0.799 vs. 0.712 clean, mean gain +0.087; up to +0.238 on Qwen3-1.7B physical_scale), exposing pervasive late-layer readout collapse. Probing boundary conditions in multi-token free-form greedy generation (Qwen3-1.7B & SmolLM2-1.7B), single-position prefill Flip-1D preserves fluent continuation NLL (0.86-1.49) but flips only 0.0%-5.6% of multi-token base-model completions (vs. 0.0% random) because subsequent generated tokens re-attend to unperturbed entity tokens in the KV cache, clarifying that sustained per-step steering is needed for multi-token generation.
findings: Steerable before decodable across 4 architectures (1.7B-7.3B, 2,688 held-out cross-lexicon pairs): At peak causal steering depth, ACE readout (0.765) exceeds Direct Logit Lens (0.727, p=6.49e-02), General-Corpus Tuned Lens (0.693, p=3.70e-02), and Domain Tuned Lens (0.708, p=4.67e-02), with mean |cos(q_l*, dW_U)| = 0.140.

Gradient-weighted ACE dominates activation-only steering baselines on 1D causal necessity (Flip-1D): Mean cross-lexicon reversal drop = +0.235 vs. CAA +0.170 (p=1.53e-04, wins 14/16), L2 Logistic Probe +0.179 (p=3.81e-03, wins 13/16), and Random Control -0.001 (p=1.53e-05).

1D causal sufficiency (Keep-1D) rescues late-layer readout collapse: Projecting the 2,048-4,096D residual stream onto only the 1D ACE axis outperforms the full unperturbed model in 16/16 cells (mean Keep-1D AUC 0.799 vs. clean final-layer 0.712, mean gain +0.087; largest rescue 0.592 -> 0.830 on Qwen3-1.7B physical_scale).

Multi-token free-form generation boundary condition (honest negative/scope result): Single-position prefill Flip-1D preserves fluent base-model continuation NLL (0.86-1.49) but flips only 0.0%-5.6% of multi-token greedy answers (vs. 0.0% random) because base models emit multi-token prefixes that re-attend to unperturbed entity tokens in the KV cache, showing sustained per-step steering is required beyond single-token logits.

(a-d) Depth trajectories with 95% bands comparing ACE 1D readout, General-Corpus Tuned Lens, Domain Tuned Lens, Direct Logit Lens, 1D causal steer drop, and |cos(q_l, ΔW_U)|. (e) Flip-1D causal necessity across all 4 models. (f) Keep-1D sufficiency & collapse rescue. (g) Causal control vs. unembedding alignment. (h) Free-form multi-token generation steering flip rate (ACE vs. Random).
limitations: Evaluated on 4 structured single-token comparative domains; free-form multi-step reasoning may recruit higher-rank subspaces.
Residual-Affine Tuned Lens was trained on pooled disjoint training-entity activations rather than a massive general pretraining corpus.
Spans 1.7B-7.2B models across 3 architectures (Qwen3, Llama, Mistral); 70B+ scaling behavior remains open.
